title: The OFF Switch Decides
endLine: Every switch is a contest: the OFF arm sets size and duration.

scenes.tts: The first film carried epinephrine's signal to P K A. Now picture cholera toxin in a gut cell. It switches nothing ON. It breaks one OFF reaction. So why can that kill within hours?
scenes.narration: The first film carried epinephrine's signal to PKA. Now picture cholera toxin in a gut cell. It switches nothing ON. It breaks one OFF reaction. So why can that kill within hours?
scenes.caption: The first film carried epinephrine's signal to PKA. Now picture cholera toxin in a gut cell. It switches nothing ON. It breaks one OFF reaction. So why can that kill within hours?
scenes.visual: The first film left no written colour map, so fix this one for the whole film and carry the first film's objects (epinephrine, receptor, cyclic AMP, PKA, glycogen to glucose). THE WORLD, kept all film: one tall cell cross-section fills about 70% of the frame height, plasma membrane across the top, a small 'schematic' tag at bottom right throughout. Down the middle of the cell runs THE RELAY ROW, four switch lamps stacked top to bottom with short labels: 'receptor' (in the membrane), 'Gs alpha', 'cyclase', 'PKA'. Below the row sits one OUTPUT TILE whose label changes with the tissue. Each lamp glows WHITE when ON and sits dim grey when OFF. Beside each lamp, a GREEN arrow from the left pushes it ON (the ON arm) and a RED arrow from the right pulls it OFF (the OFF arm). Colour by concept: epinephrine ORANGE ball outside the membrane; cyclic AMP GOLD dots; glucose units pale BLUE dots; chloride and water CYAN drops; cholera toxin PURPLE. The row counts as one object; never more than six labelled things on screen. MOTION: on the link-back sentence, the cell is labelled 'liver cell' and the output tile reads 'glucose'; an ORANGE epinephrine ball docks on the receptor, the lamps light WHITE top to bottom, GOLD dots spill from the cyclase, the PKA lamp lights, and pale BLUE glucose dots stream from the output tile. Then all lamps dim. On 'gut cell', the cell label morphs to 'gut cell' and the output tile to 'chloride and water'. A PURPLE toxin token drifts in and settles on the RED OFF arrow beside 'Gs alpha'; that red arrow cracks and goes grey. The Gs alpha lamp lights WHITE and stays lit; GOLD dots pour from the cyclase; CYAN drops stream out of the output tile and off the bottom of the cell. Large white text at top: 'Why is this deadly?'

Title 'The OFF Switch Decides' fades in at top for 2 s while the question text fades out. The cracked RED arrow and PURPLE toxin fade away, the cell label returns to 'liver cell', the output tile to 'glucose', and all lamps sit dim grey. GOLD dots drift slowly in the cytosol.

scenes.tts: Take one switch, Gs alpha. The receptor pushes it ON, swapping G D P for G T P. Its own G T P ase pulls it OFF, a built-in timer. How much is ON is a contest between them.
scenes.narration: Take one switch, Gs alpha. The receptor pushes it ON, swapping GDP for GTP. Its own GTPase pulls it OFF, a built-in timer. How much is ON is a contest between them.
scenes.caption: Take one switch, Gs alpha. The receptor pushes it ON, swapping GDP for GTP. Its own GTPase pulls it OFF, a built-in timer. How much is ON is a contest between them.
scenes.visual: Camera eases in so the 'Gs alpha' lamp and its two arrows fill the middle of the frame; the rest of the row stays visible but dimmer above and below. On 'pushes it ON', an ORANGE epinephrine ball sits on the receptor and the GREEN arrow pushes: a small token labelled 'GDP' leaves the lamp and one labelled 'GTP' enters; the lamp lights WHITE. On 'pulls it OFF', a small RED stopwatch icon labelled 'timer' appears on the RED arrow and counts down; when it runs out the GTP token turns into GDP and the lamp dims. On 'contest', the two arrows push and pull in turn; the lamp flickers between WHITE and grey, settling at a steady half glow. A thin tug-of-war rope between the GREEN and RED arrows appears, labelled 'ON versus OFF'.

scenes.tts: While Gs alpha holds G T P, its cyclase makes cyclic A M P. In round numbers, ten a second for about ten seconds makes about one hundred. So an enzyme's gain is its speed, times how long it stays ON. Slow the timer, and the same cyclase makes more.
scenes.narration: While Gs alpha holds GTP, its cyclase makes cyclic AMP. In round numbers, 10 a second for about 10 seconds makes about 100. So an enzyme's gain is its speed, times how long it stays ON. Slow the timer, and the same cyclase makes more.
scenes.caption: While Gs alpha holds GTP, its cyclase makes cyclic AMP. In round numbers, 10 a second for about 10 seconds makes about 100. So an enzyme's gain is its speed, times how long it stays ON. Slow the timer, and the same cyclase makes more.
scenes.visual: Camera slides down one step so the 'Gs alpha' and 'cyclase' lamps fill the frame. Both glow WHITE. GOLD cyclic AMP dots pop out of the cyclase at a steady rate and drop into a counter box at right labelled 'cyclic AMP made'. Above the counter, a WHITE bar labelled 'ON time' fills over 10 seconds of on-screen clock (sped up to match the narration) while the counter ticks 10, 20, 30 up to 100: computed from 10 per second times 10 seconds. When the bar is full, the RED timer on Gs alpha runs out, Gs alpha dims, the cyclase dims and the dots stop. A label forms under the counter: 'gain = speed × ON time'. On 'slow the timer', the RED stopwatch visibly slows, the ON-time bar stretches longer (schematic, no number) and the counter climbs past 100 with no new number shown, tagged 'more'. Then the counter resets.

scenes.tts: Each switch down the row has its own ON and OFF arms. And the gains multiply. In teaching numbers, one epinephrine molecule ends as tens of millions of glucose units. Real gains differ between cell types.
scenes.narration: Each switch down the row has its own ON and OFF arms. And the gains multiply. In teaching numbers, one epinephrine molecule ends as tens of millions of glucose units. Real gains differ between cell types.
scenes.caption: Each switch down the row has its own ON and OFF arms. And the gains multiply. In teaching numbers, one epinephrine molecule ends as tens of millions of glucose units. Real gains differ between cell types.
scenes.visual: Camera pulls back to the full cell and row. On 'its own ON and OFF arms', each lamp's GREEN and RED arrows pulse in turn, top to bottom. On 'the gains multiply', one ORANGE epinephrine ball docks and the lamps cascade ON; a single running-total counter at right labelled 'running total' steps through values computed from the lesson's teaching gains (×10, ×1, ×100, ×½, ×10, ×10, ×1,000): 10, 10, 1,000, 500, 5,000, 50,000, 50,000,000. Pale BLUE glucose dots flood from the output tile, filling the lower cell. The counter's last value relabels to 'tens of millions'. A small tag beside it: 'teaching values'.

scenes.tts: The one idea: every switch is pushed ON by one reaction and pulled OFF by another. The OFF reaction sets how long each switch stays ON, and so how big the answer gets. And once the signal leaves, the response fades at about the pace of the slowest OFF step.
scenes.narration: The one idea: every switch is pushed ON by one reaction and pulled OFF by another. The OFF reaction sets how long each switch stays ON, and so how big the answer gets. And once the signal leaves, the response fades at about the pace of the slowest OFF step.

scenes.visual: All four lamps glow WHITE with their GREEN and RED arrows visible. On 'pushed ON', every GREEN arrow brightens together; on 'pulled OFF', every RED arrow brightens together. A banner at top: 'ON arm versus OFF arm'. On 'how long', each lamp shows a short WHITE ON-time bar beside it; on 'how big', the bars feed into the running-total counter, which glows. On 'once the signal leaves', the ORANGE epinephrine ball lifts off the receptor and floats away. The lamps fade at different speeds (schematic): one has a visibly slow RED timer, tagged 'slowest OFF step', and the glucose stream from the output tile thins at the same slow pace as that lamp, not faster. No numbers or axes on this fade.

scenes.tts: Now cholera. The toxin chemically modifies Gs alpha, so it can no longer cut its G T P. Gs is locked ON. Cyclic A M P never stops, and chloride and water pour into the intestine. Severe dehydration can kill within hours.
scenes.narration: Now cholera. The toxin chemically modifies Gs alpha, so it can no longer cut its GTP. Gs is locked ON. Cyclic AMP never stops, and chloride and water pour into the intestine. Severe dehydration can kill within hours.
scenes.caption: Now cholera. The toxin chemically modifies Gs alpha, so it can no longer cut its GTP. Gs is locked ON. Cyclic AMP never stops, and chloride and water pour into the intestine. Severe dehydration can kill within hours.
scenes.visual: Return to the hook picture: the cell label morphs to 'gut cell' and the output tile to 'chloride and water'. The PURPLE toxin token settles on the RED arrow beside 'Gs alpha'; the stopwatch on that arrow freezes and the arrow cracks and goes grey, tagged 'OFF arm broken'. The Gs alpha lamp locks WHITE, with a small padlock icon labelled 'locked ON'. GOLD dots pour from the cyclase without stopping. On 'chloride and water', CYAN drops stream from the output tile out of the bottom of the cell, a growing CYAN pool forming below it labelled 'into intestine'. The other lamps' arrows stay intact.

scenes.tts: Another stuck switch. P K A sits clamped by regulatory subunits until cyclic A M P frees it. In some cases of Cushing's syndrome, its active subunit cannot bind the clamp. Every OFF enzyme still works. With no cyclic A M P, is P K A ON or OFF?
scenes.narration: Another stuck switch. PKA sits clamped by regulatory subunits until cyclic AMP frees it. In some cases of Cushing's syndrome, its active subunit cannot bind the clamp. Every OFF enzyme still works. With no cyclic AMP, is PKA ON or OFF?
scenes.caption: Another stuck switch. PKA sits clamped by regulatory subunits until cyclic AMP frees it. In some cases of Cushing's syndrome, its active subunit cannot bind the clamp. Every OFF enzyme still works. With no cyclic AMP, is PKA ON or OFF?
scenes.visual: The cholera story ends: the PURPLE toxin, padlock, cracked arrow and CYAN pool fade, the Gs alpha RED arrow is whole again and all lamps are dim. Camera slides down to the 'PKA' lamp, which now fills the middle of the frame. Its lamp is drawn as two plain bracket shapes labelled 'clamp' holding a WHITE core labelled 'active subunit' (simple shapes, no molecular structure). On 'until cyclic AMP frees it', GOLD dots land on the clamp, the brackets open and the core lights WHITE; then the dots leave and the clamp closes, the core dimming. On 'Cushing's syndrome', the cell label morphs to 'adrenal cell', the output tile relabels to 'cortisol', and a small tag reads 'Cushing's (some cases)'. The core's edge changes shape so it no longer fits the clamp. On 'every OFF enzyme still works', the RED arrows on the lamps above PKA glow intact, while PKA's clamp stays open. All GOLD dots drain away. Question card at top in white: 'No cyclic AMP: ON or OFF?'

Deliberate thinking pause. The question card stays. The misshapen WHITE core sits beside the open, empty clamp; no GOLD dots anywhere; the RED arrows glow steadily. The core trembles slightly and its glow is held at a neutral half-brightness so it does not give away the answer. Ambient motion only: faint cytosol shimmer.

scenes.tts: ON. P K A escapes its clamp, and cortisol production runs with no hormone telling it to. Nothing is wrong with the OFF enzymes here. The switch no longer needs its ON signal.
scenes.narration: ON. PKA escapes its clamp, and cortisol production runs with no hormone telling it to. Nothing is wrong with the OFF enzymes here. The switch no longer needs its ON signal.
scenes.caption: ON. PKA escapes its clamp, and cortisol production runs with no hormone telling it to. Nothing is wrong with the OFF enzymes here. The switch no longer needs its ON signal.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves into a clear white 'ON'. The misshapen core lights full WHITE and drifts free of the empty clamp. The output tile 'cortisol' pulses steadily, emitting small WHITE output dots. The receptor stays empty, with no ORANGE ball, and no GOLD dots appear: a tag 'no hormone' sits by the receptor. On 'nothing is wrong with the OFF enzymes', the RED arrows on the lamps above PKA pulse intact once. On 'no longer needs its ON signal', the GREEN arrow beside PKA fades to a faint ghost while the lamp stays lit.

scenes.tts: So a switch sticks ON when it loses its OFF reaction, or stops needing its ON signal. The contest can also tip the other way. Weaken an ON arm, as in insulin resistance, and the response is too small.
scenes.narration: So a switch sticks ON when it loses its OFF reaction, or stops needing its ON signal. The contest can also tip the other way. Weaken an ON arm, as in insulin resistance, and the response is too small.
scenes.caption: So a switch sticks ON when it loses its OFF reaction, or stops needing its ON signal. The contest can also tip the other way. Weaken an ON arm, as in insulin resistance, and the response is too small.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full row; the PKA core returns to its clamp, the cell label returns to 'liver cell' and the output tile reads 'glucose' again. Two small labelled icons appear at left in turn: a cracked RED arrow labelled 'lost OFF arm' (beside Gs alpha), then a faded GREEN arrow under a lit lamp labelled 'needs no ON signal' (beside PKA). On 'the other way', a separate generic switch icon appears at left, outside this row, with a thin, weak GREEN arrow and a strong RED arrow; it barely glows. It becomes the third icon: 'weak ON arm', with a small tag 'insulin resistance' and its own thin output trickle, labelled 'too little'. Then all three icons line up at left.

scenes.tts: So the OFF reactions decide how big a cell's answer is, and how long it lasts. When one fails, the answer runs on without the signal.
scenes.narration: So the OFF reactions decide how big a cell's answer is, and how long it lasts. When one fails, the answer runs on without the signal.
scenes.caption: So the OFF reactions decide how big a cell's answer is, and how long it lasts. When one fails, the answer runs on without the signal.
scenes.visual: The three icons fade. All four lamps are whole, GREEN and RED arrows intact. On 'the OFF reactions', every RED arrow brightens together. On 'how big', the running-total counter reappears and glows; on 'how long', the WHITE ON-time bars beside the lamps glow. On 'when one fails', the RED arrow beside Gs alpha cracks once more and its lamp stays WHITE while the ORANGE epinephrine ball floats away from the receptor; GOLD dots keep spilling from the cyclase with no hormone present.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (the relay row with its GREEN and RED arrows gently pushing and pulling, GOLD dots drifting). Large white text, centred: 'Every switch is a contest: the OFF arm sets size and duration.'
